author: agent
text:
THE `[:200]` HERE IS A DISPLAY BOUND. IT MUST NEVER BE WHAT ROT COMPARES. If you change how comments are harvested, keep those two jobs apart - they were the same value until 0.61.0 and it cost the project a whole class of forced confirms.

WHAT HAPPENED. Comments ride in agent payloads, so each is truncated to 200 characters. comment_hash was then built from those truncated strings, so comment-rot detection could only ever see the first 200 characters of a docstring. On this repo's own map that is 307 of 785 commented entities - 39% - carrying a comment at the cut. This repo's docstrings run past 1,600 characters routinely; the load-bearing part of a docstring is never the first sentence, which says what a function returns. It is the rest, which says why, and which is the part that rots.

BOTH DIRECTIONS WERE WRONG.

  A REAL FIX PAST THE CUT DID NOT CLEAR THE FLAG. Found on metadata.for_display while following the release ceremony: its docstring was rewritten to describe newly added behaviour, the hash did not move, rot stayed lit. The only way out was to write a `confirm` attesting that a docstring was accurate - a docstring that had genuinely just been corrected. That is confirm volume manufactured by a bug, entirely separately from the workflow cause diagnosed the same session.

  A COSMETIC EDIT INSIDE THE CUT DID CLEAR IT. Fix a typo in the opening sentence and rot goes quiet on a docstring that is still wrong for its remaining 1,400 characters. A false 'fresh', which this project treats as the more serious failure of the two.

THE FIX. Every harvest site now carries `h`, a digest of the FULL text (indexer._ctext_hash), and comment_hash is built from `h` with a fallback to `text` so pre-0.61 maps stay readable. The digest rather than the full string because comments are stored per entity in coordinates.json and banking whole docstrings there would inflate every map. PARSE_SCHEMA_VERSION went 12 -> 13: a cache warmed at 12 replays comments with no `h`, the fallback fires, and the bug returns silently on every file that did not happen to change.

MIGRATION, and it is the safe direction. Re-deriving the hash changes it for every entity, and the rot rule reads `prev_ch != comment_hash -> rot cleared`. So the first re-index after this clears the existing rot backlog once rather than mass-flagging false rot. This repo's backlog was 0 at the time, so nothing was lost here; a repo pulling 0.61.0 with a real backlog gets one free pass on it.

WHY IT SURVIVED THIS LONG. It is invisible to every test that checks behaviour, because the behaviour is correct for any comment under 200 characters - which is all of them in a hand-built fixture. It took a docstring of 1,672 characters, which only real code has (lesson 5), and it took the ceremony actually being followed rather than short-circuited.
